findings.reason: a case whose base arm passes measures nothing, so the node would ship and gate a duplicate memo while believing it had proven the change.
findings.text: §42's second case requires that "two refreshes over an unchanged run call git for that run's review tier once", with the control "at the base revision … the second refresh calls git again", but base already memoises that tier: `obligations._review_tier_for_duty` (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:2044-2049`) returns through `file_memo.memoized_key("obligation_review_tier", _review_tier_key(...), …)`, and `tests/test_a_review_duty_reads_its_run_review_once.py::test_each_review_is_read_once_until_its_entries_move` already asserts at base that an unchanged pass re-reads nothing — so the control is green at base and the case cannot distinguish head from base

findings.reason: the instrument to falsify it exists at base (`review_records.review_store_tick()` is defined at `reckon/crew/review_records.py:47-57` and no non-review caller installs it, so base globs per item), and without that arm the node cannot show its third change is what fixed the glob.
findings.text: §42's third measure, that a refresh over many duty items "calls `directory.glob` on the review store at most once per tick", carries no negative control: the stated control names only the blocked-derivation and repeated-git cases, so the store-glob half of the gate rests on an assertion that could pass on the unfixed code

findings.reason: this plan already narrowed §32 from two deliverables to one for the same reason, and narrowing §42 to the two changes that are not already present at base leaves one coherent node with one verdict.
findings.text: §42 puts three independently closable deliverables on one node — publish phase transitions before duty derivation, memoise the review-tier git calls, and install the per-tick review store — each with its own measure and its own negative control, so one verdict cannot close all three and a partially-failing gate reads as failing the whole section

findings.reason: the node would spend its effort layering a second memo over a working one instead of measuring what the tick actually still costs, which is the phase ordering and the store glob.
findings.text: deliverable (2) states that `_run_review_tier`'s git calls are to be "memoised per (run id, head revision) for the life of the station process, so a run whose head has not moved costs no git process on a later tick", but that steady-state property already holds at base through the bounded memo on `_review_tier_key` (row, pointer, head, tree), so the section re-states an existing guard as a fix and its cited root cause (git per run per tick) overstates what remains

findings.reason: the done-when beneath it is phrased as three observables that can each fail, and naming the write paths is this plan's established house idiom in every section, so rewriting it changes style rather than the endpoint the node is held to.
findings.text: the deliverable fixes implementation rather than the endpoint: it names the reordering of two internal stages, the exact memo key "(run id, head revision)", the direction to install the per-tick store, and the named modules to change, so the plan asserts a method a later reader cannot check against an observable
